locator: I q.10 a.1 co.: Quod vero est omnino immutabile, sicut nec successionem, ita nec principium aut finem habere potest
interpretation: Things measured by time have beginning and end in time, because in whatever is moved there is some beginning and some end; what is altogether immutable can have neither succession nor beginning nor end. 'Omnino immutabile' is taken in q.9's sense, which q.9 a.2 contrasts with creatures mutable through a power in another; the sentence does not itself say that whatever begins has potency in its subject.
